name: Light-canvas voice-agent launch (music only): two-tone headlines beside the interface, the beat drops when the product appears

source.creator: unknown

rights.attribution: Unknown creator; supplied by the user as a private study reference.

brand_assets.description: Product wordmark and the product name inside headlines
Call card, chat, calendar, leads, dashboard and booking interfaces

rights.notes: Rights unverified. AI voice-agent launch; reuse the two-tone headline grammar, the light single page and the beat-drop-on-product principle only, with original copy and interface.

analysis.inspected_by: agent (GitHub Copilot, Session F) using the reference-analyst workflow
analysis.method: Viewed overview (63 frames), the motion sheet (4 windows at 10 fps, 26.92-39.68 s), the audio panel, the listen sheet (7 phrases, 10 accent hits); 30 fps strips at 1.50-3.00 s and 40.90-42.00 s and a 15 fps strip at 17.40-19.40 s (21 headline-word arrivals measured against onsets). No transitions sheet (no detected boundaries). Strips at 5.0-6.5, 11.1-12.0, 23.4-24.6, 38.7-39.5 and 44.0-45.4 s were generated but not viewed. Signal features and Windows en-US dictation; nothing was listened to.
analysis.coverage: Full 47.57 s (1280x720, 30 fps); three headline builds at 15-30 fps; the rest at 0.75 s sampling.

concept.observed: A launch for an AI voice agent that answers a business's calls: a missed call is a missed client; the agent answers, books into the calendar, captures leads, reports on calls, offers a booking link and QR code; end line and wordmark.
concept.interpreted: Problem, product, four features, promise: one argument on one page.

communication_style.observed: Music only, despite the title; the argument is carried by two-line headlines beside the interface.

palette.observed: Off-white (#f8f8f8, 88%) with soft grey shadows; black type; one accent per headline (red for the problem, blue for a feature, teal for the promise); a warm beige panel for the booking page.

typography.observed: Medium-weight grotesque headlines in sentence case, 2 lines; line 2 ends on the key word in the accent colour; tiny interface type; a centred wordmark.

composition.observed: Headline left at about 5-35% of the width, vertically centred; interface card or window right; full-width app windows for the calendar, leads and dashboard.

motion.observed: Headline words fade in with a blur, a fixed 0.13 s apart (median; range 0.06-0.17 s), the accent word last; a call card rings, turns to missed and a list of missed calls stacks under it; chat bubbles and a waveform build (6.4-10.9 s); calendar events pop into slots and a new booking is outlined in teal (14.7-16.2 s); KPI counters and an area chart (29.8-33.6 s); a booking page with a month calendar and a QR code (34.3-40.4 s); the wordmark types in (44.9-46.4 s).

transitions.observed: None detected in 47.6 s: one light page. Sections change by dissolving the headline and interface out and the next in over about 0.2-0.7 s (5.26-5.46, 11.0-11.7, 17.6-17.8, 23.8-24.5, 34.0-34.4 s); the frame is empty at 44.17 s before the wordmark.
transitions.interpreted: Light canvas, no cuts: the corpus pattern for light product films holds over 47 s.

timing_and_rhythm.observed: Sections of about 5.3, 5.7, 6.3, 6.5, 10.0, 6.5 and 7 s; headlines held 3-5 s complete.

sound_design.observed: -15.9 LUFS, LRA 5.6 LU, true peak -4.9 dBTP; tempo 66.3 bpm (medium); 241 onsets; 49 accents (61.8/min); no boundaries, so no accents-on-cuts measure. Two parts: a sparse intro (0-13.4 s, median level -24.6 dB, onsets 0.2-1.0 s apart) under the problem and the first feature, then at 13.42 s the full beat enters, +7.3 dB (median -17.3 dB over 13.6-46 s, onsets every 0.11-0.23 s), as the calendar window fills the frame. Accents sit on a 0.88-0.91 s grid (one beat at 66 bpm) with 0.44 and 0.23 s subdivisions. The strongest accents in the intro land on the first headline (1.79 s; 2.69 s just after it completes), the missed-call list (3.58 s), the headline swap (5.36 s) and the chat and booking elements (6.27, 7.15, 7.62, 8.06, 8.29, 8.73, 8.94, 9.85 s). No silences; head -7.3 dB, tail +0.5 dB; the level falls only in the last 0.5 s. Accents may be part of the music.
sound_design.interpreted: The arrangement marks the turn from problem to product: the beat arrives with the product.

narration.observed: None, although the title suggested a voice. Dictation: 29 raw words, 11 confident, 7 phrases, and every confident word is the same single letter; 0.92 words/s while 'speaking', 20 words/min over 14.17-47.31 s, 6 pauses (median 3570 ms, max 6060 ms), thirds 0.45/0.36/0.18 words/s; no boundaries to test against pauses. The phrase frames show the calendar, a headline with the lead card, the dashboard, the booking page, the end line and the wordmark, with no speaker; the spectrogram shows a steady music texture without speech formants; syllabic share 0.37 (corpus median 0.34).
narration.interpreted: Recogniser noise over music: these numbers are not a narration pace.

captions.observed: No captions. Copy lanes: the two-line headline left of the interface (lines of 2-4 words, held 3-5 s), and a one-line label centred under the full-width app windows (about 93% of the height; plate not resolvable at sheet size). Headline words against music onsets (21 measured at 15-30 fps): 10 within 50 ms against chance 0.51, offsets -220 to +270 ms: the per-word cadence is fixed, not locked to the music. The accent-coloured last word lands within 10 ms of an onset in 2 of 3 lines (18.80 vs 18.81 s; 41.97 vs 41.98 s) and 60 ms early in the third (2.40 vs 2.46 s).
captions.interpreted: A fixed 0.13 s per-word cadence reads as calm typing; only the payoff word may be placed on the beat.

scenes.observed: A call rings and is missed; the problem headline; a list of missed calls.
The agent answers: waveform, chat, a booking confirmed.
A calendar fills; the beat enters at 13.42 s; a new booking is highlighted.
Leads table, lead detail, a dashboard with counters and a chart.
A booking page; one link, one QR code.
End line in two colours; empty frame; the wordmark types in.

moments.observed: The level steps up 7.3 dB as the full beat enters, at the moment the calendar window fills the frame.
moments.interpreted: Sound marks the turn from the problem to the product.

uncertainties: Whether the step at 13.42 s is the music's own drop or an edit to the picture
Whether the label under the app windows sits on a plate
Exact word times in the 17.4-19.4 s strip (15 fps: +/- 33 ms)
